title: The stub claude of a dispatched worker is an extensionless /bin/sh script, so on Windows the real claude stays reachable with no warning
goal: bl_dispatch.paid_stub(iid, platform=None) and guard_spend(bl, iid, env, platform=None) take the platform (default sys.platform): on win32 guard_spend writes a claude.cmd stub into the stub-bin directory (@echo off, the message on stderr, exit /b 2) and puts that directory first on PATH, and on any other platform it writes the extensionless /bin/sh claude as it does today, so a worker on Windows meets the stub when it calls claude by name
repro_reason: the behaviour is Windows-only and this host cannot run it: only the source can be read

run:
import sys,tempfile,types,subprocess,pathlib,os
try:
    sys.path.insert(0,"_tools");import bl_dispatch as d
    r=pathlib.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp());subprocess.run(["git","init","-q",str(r)],check=True)
    bl=types.SimpleNamespace(root=r,items={"BG-aaaaaaaa":{}})
    env=d.guard_spend(bl,"BG-aaaaaaaa",{"PATH":"/usr/bin"},platform="win32")
    s=pathlib.Path(env["PATH"].split(os.pathsep)[0]);t=(s/"claude.cmd").read_text()
    ok=t.startswith("@echo off") and "exit /b 2" in t and "BG-aaaaaaaa" in t and s.name==d.STUB_DIR_NAME
except Exception as e:
    print(type(e).__name__,e);ok=False
print(ok);sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)
